Help build the sim

The talent trees here cover every class, but the DPS sim and BiS lists so far only exist for Barbarian (Brutality & Headhunting). I'd love help extending it. If you know a spec well and want it simmed, here's what's needed to model it accurately.

Core setup

  • Class + spec name, and the primary resource (rage / energy / mana / focus / runes / combo points…).
  • Weapon setup the spec uses: two-hand, dual-wield, thrown, or ranged.
  • Any stance / form / aura that changes damage or resource behaviour.

Resource system

  • Starting and max resource, and how it regenerates (per second, on auto-hit, on crit…).
  • Every generator and how much it grants; every spender and its cost.

Abilities — the big one (for every damaging ability)

  • Base damage or coefficient: flat, "X% weapon damage", or a spell coefficient.
  • Attack-power / spell-power scaling.
  • Resource cost, cooldown, cast time (instant / cast / channel), and whether it's on the GCD.
  • Physical or magic (so armor / resistance is applied correctly), and whether it can crit.
  • Targets: single-target, or cleave / AoE + how many and any damage falloff.
  • Conditional bonuses: execute range, bonus vs bleeding/poisoned targets, stacking buffs, etc.

Auto-attacks

  • Main-hand (and off-hand) weapon min/max damage and speed; thrown / ranged if relevant.

Talents & choice nodes

  • Every DPS-relevant talent: exact effect (%/flat, proc chance + internal cooldown), what it modifies, and ranks. Note pick-one choice nodes.

Buffs, procs & cooldowns

  • Self-buffs, trinket / set procs, and major cooldowns: effect, duration, cooldown, and when they're active (e.g. enrage windows).

Stat scaling (server values)

  • How attack power is derived from Strength / Agility, and the rating→% conversions this server uses for crit, haste, hit, expertise, and armor penetration.
  • Any custom formulas or recent balance changes — CoA differs from retail.

Rotation

  • The intended ability priority, and anything that reshuffles it (procs, execute phase…).

The more precise the numbers, the better the sim — tooltip values and in-game testing are ideal, but "roughly X" is a fine starting point. Screenshots of tooltips and talent trees help a lot.
